allowed_bases.THIRD_PARTY_PROFILE: A profile or entry the entity controls on a host it does not own (a social profile, Wikidata, Crunchbase). source_url must be off the entity host and must name the entity, so a profile cannot be claimed on resemblance alone.

why_no_third_party_record: Checked 26 October 2026, from the handles the entity would own: pinterest.com/theindustryguides and linkedin.com/company/theindustryguides do not exist (Pinterest answers 200 for any handle, so the body was compared against a known-live account and a deliberately bogus one; the bogus handle and theindustryguides both returned the "user not found" body). crunchbase.com refuses robots. x.com/industryguides resolves but is someone else's account and is NOT claimed. The entity publishes no social profile, so there is no THIRD_PARTY_PROFILE record to make; when one is created it is registered here (the weekly watch does it). Re-checked 30 October 2026: linkedin.com/company/theindustryguides and /the-industry-guides 404, youtube.com/@theindustryguides 404, github.com/theindustryguides 404, facebook.com/theindustryguides 400, theindustryguides.substack.com 404, Bluesky theindustryguides.com "Profile not found", no Wikidata entity. The pending profiles are listed in entity.json profiles_pending and rechecked weekly by entity-backlink-watch.yml.
self_reference_prohibited: No VERIFIED record may sit on entity_host (30 Oct 2026). FIRST_PARTY_ENTITY_PAGE was removed from allowed_bases, so a first-party record cannot be re-verified; scripts/lib/entity_graph_check.js and validate_network_crawler_contract.js both fail on one.
